body.statement:
Put \(q=Sd\).  Suppose \(\delta_0<1/2\), \(B^4>q^2\), \(c_\Sigma I_q\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_q\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0\) for every \(s\).  For every \(\eta\in(0,1)\), there are constants \(c_\eta>0\) and \(N_\eta<\infty\), depending only on \(\eta\) and the fixed class parameters, such that for every \(N\ge N_\eta\) there are probability laws \(G_0,G_1\) on \(\mathbb R^q\) with means \(z_0,z_1\), respectively, common covariance \(\Sigma\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_{G_v}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z-z_v)\|_2^4\le B^4,
 \qquad
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z_1-z_0)\|_2^2=c_\eta^2,
 \qquad v\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The displacement \(z_1-z_0\) has one nonzero coordinate, \(z_1\) obeys the same \(\delta_0\)-interior restriction, and the product laws satisfy \(\|G_1^{\otimes N}-G_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1-\eta\).
body.proof_tex:
Let \(q=Sd\), and choose a coordinate vector \(e\) with sign pointing from the corresponding coordinate of \(z_0\) toward \(1/2\).  A displacement \(ve\) with \(0\le v\le1/2-\delta_0\) therefore remains in the \(\delta_0\)-trimmed cube.  Put
\[
 w=\frac{\Sigma^{-1/2}e}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}
\]
and choose an orthogonal matrix \(O\) sending the first coordinate vector to \(w\).  Fix
\[
 0<\epsilon< B^4-q^2,
 \qquad c_0=(1+\epsilon)^{1/2}.
\]
For a real number \(u\) near zero, define a scalar random variable \(A_u\) on \(\{-c_0,0,c_0\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2c_0^2}+\frac{u}{2c_0},\qquad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2c_0^2}-\frac{u}{2c_0},\qquad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{c_0^2}.
\tag{1}
\]
At \(u=0\) all three probabilities are strictly positive.  Hence they remain probabilities for \(|u|\le u_0\), for some \(u_0>0\).  Direct calculation from (1) gives
\[
 \mathbb E A_u=u,
 \qquad \mathbb E A_u^2=1+u^2,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(A_u)=1.
\tag{2}
\]
Let \(R_2,\ldots,R_q\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of \(A_u\), and set
\[
 V_u=O(A_u,R_2,\ldots,R_q)^{\top}.
\]
Equations (1)--(2) imply
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=uw,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(V_u)=I_q.
\tag{3}
\]
Orthogonal invariance of Euclidean norm and independence give
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_u-uw\|_2^4
 =\mathbb E(A_u-u)^4+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2.
\tag{4}
\]
At \(u=0\), the right side of (4) is \(c_0^2+q^2-1=q^2+\epsilon<B^4\).  It is continuous in \(u\), so, after decreasing \(u_0\), it is at most \(B^4\) whenever \(|u|\le u_0\).

Define \(G_u\) as the law of
\[
 Z_u=z_0+\Sigma^{1/2}V_u.
\]
By (3), its mean and covariance are
\[
 z(u)=z_0+u\Sigma^{1/2}w
     =z_0+\frac{u}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}e,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(Z_u)=\Sigma,
\tag{5}
\]
and (4) is exactly the required standardized fourth moment about \(z(u)\).

It remains to control overlap.  The Hellinger affinity between \(G_0\) and \(G_u\) equals
\[
 a(u)=\sum_{r\in\{-,0,+\}}\{p_r(0)p_r(u)\}^{1/2},
\]
because the Rademacher coordinates, the rotation, and the invertible linear transformation are common.  On a sufficiently small compact neighborhood of zero, the three square-root terms have bounded second derivatives.  Moreover, \(a(0)=1\) and
\[
 a'(0)=\frac12\sum_r p_r'(0)=0.
\]
Taylor's theorem therefore gives \(a(u)\ge1-Cu^2\).  For \(CNu^2\le1/2\),
\[
 a(u)^N\ge(1-Cu^2)^N\ge\exp(-2CNu^2).
\tag{6}
\]
For any two dominated laws with densities \(p,g\), Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(|p-g|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt g|(\sqrt p+\sqrt g)\) yields
\[
 \|P-G\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\left\{1-\left(\int\sqrt{pg}\right)^2\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{7}
\]
Choose \(c_\eta>0\) small enough that the right side of (7), after using (6) with \(u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}\), is at most \(1-\eta\).  Also take \(c_\eta\le1\).  Equations (5)--(7) then give
\[
 \|G_{c_\eta N^{-1/2}}^{\otimes N}-G_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le1-\eta,\qquad
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}\{z(c_\eta N^{-1/2})-z_0\}\|_2^2=c_\eta^2.
\]
Finally, ellipticity gives \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2^{-1}\le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\).  Thus (5) remains in the trimmed cube for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Taking \(G_0=G_{u=0}\), \(G_1=G_{u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}}\), and enlarging \(N_\eta\) to enforce all preceding bounds proves the lemma.
body.justification: This finite-support construction supplies an arbitrarily overlapping root-\(N\) donor-location pair for every prescribed full covariance, rather than importing a Gaussian location family that can violate bounded fourth-moment slack.
body.gap: Strict slack \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\) are necessary for this regular location construction.
body.consumer: The conditional minimax converse and the uniformly honest expected-length donor converse use the pair with different overlap levels.
